history.summary: AMBIGUOUS IDENTITY - the CSV name 'Shri Siddh Baba Balak Nath Temple, Yamunanagar' (note: CSV spelling 'Siddh' vs common 'Sidh') has no unique documented referent; it is mapped here to the Baba Balak Nath Mandir at Farkhpur, Yamunanagar (1014-B, Farkhpur), with ambiguity clearly flagged. Another local candidate is the Baba Balak Nath Mandir in Laxmi Nagar Camp, Yamunanagar (Justdial listing: Gali No 6, opens 9:00 am-9:30 pm daily). A same-named 'Shri Sidh Baba Balak Nath Ji Ka Mandir' also exists at Shivalik Colony, Ambala (yappe.in) - documented but in the wrong district. These appear to be local neighborhood shrines of Baba Balak Nath, the siddha saint venerated across Himachal/Haryana (traditionally held as a manifestation of Kartikeya; principal seat is the Deotsidh cave temple in Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh). No founding history, built date or festival calendar is published for this local mandir; festival list is left empty rather than invented. Coordinates are POI-level from a place listing (30.130388, 77.239353) and should be treated as approximate.

town_description: Farkhpur is a locality adjoining Yamunanagar city in Yamunanagar district, Haryana, on the edge of the industrial Yamunanagar-Jagadhri urban area. Yamunanagar is known for its plywood and timber industries and lies on the banks of the Western Yamuna Canal.
